name: Kathmandu Valley
tagline: Three royal cities and seven UNESCO zones
meta_description: Kathmandu Valley tours: Pashupatinath, Boudhanath, Bhaktapur, Patan, Nagarkot sunrise and Nepal packages from Kathmandu, with prices in INR and USD.
summary: The Kathmandu Valley is where almost every Nepal trip starts and where most of its history sits: three former royal cities, seven UNESCO monument zones, Pashupatinath and Boudhanath, and hill towns like Nagarkot and Dhulikhel with Himalayan views. Plan two to four nights, best from October to April.
intro: The valley is a bowl about 25 km across at roughly 1,400 m, ringed by forested hills that climb to 2,732 m at Shivapuri. Inside it sit three old city-states, Kathmandu, Patan and Bhaktapur, which were rival Newar kingdoms until Prithvi Narayan Shah united Nepal in the 1760s. Their palace squares, pagoda temples and carved courtyards survive within a few kilometres of each other, so in two full days you can see more listed heritage than in most countries.

Seven monument zones make up the Kathmandu Valley World Heritage Site, inscribed by UNESCO in 1979: the three Durbar Squares, the Hindu temple complexes of Pashupatinath and Changu Narayan, and the Buddhist stupas of Swayambhunath and Boudhanath. The 2015 Gorkha earthquake brought down several temples, and the rebuilding has been careful and slow; Kasthamandap reopened in 2021, and scaffolding still appears around some monuments. We plan routes so that you see restored work and living ritual, not just ruins.

Faith here is daily and public. Hindu pilgrims from India queue for darshan of Pashupatinath and attend the evening aarti on the Bagmati, while Tibetan families circle Boudhanath at dusk spinning prayer wheels. Many shrines serve both Hindus and Buddhists, and festivals such as Indra Jatra, Bisket Jatra, Dashain and Tihar fill the squares. For pilgrims the valley pairs naturally with Manakamana and Muktinath further west.

Above the valley floor, Nagarkot at about 2,175 m and Dhulikhel at about 1,550 m give sunrise views across 300 km of the Himalaya from Langtang towards Everest on clear days, and Chandragiri's cable car lifts you to 2,551 m in about 10 minutes. Kathmandu is also the gateway for Everest mountain flights and for most of our multi-region tours to Pokhara, Chitwan and beyond, so even short trips usually begin and end here.

highlights.title: Three Durbar Squares in two days
highlights.text: Kathmandu, Patan and Bhaktapur each kept their royal palace square, with pagoda temples, stone fountains and carved windows. They lie within 15 km of each other, so a guided two-day plan covers all three, plus Bhaktapur's Nyatapola, the valley's tallest temple at five storeys.

highlights.title: Pashupatinath darshan and aarti
highlights.text: Nepal's holiest Shiva temple stands on the Bagmati, about 5 km east of Thamel. Hindu visitors enter for darshan; everyone can watch the evening aarti from the river terraces, where priests wave lamps to music as dusk falls. Maha Shivaratri brings hundreds of thousands of pilgrims.

highlights.title: Boudhanath and Swayambhunath stupas
highlights.text: Boudhanath is one of the largest stupas in Asia and the centre of Kathmandu's Tibetan community, best at dusk during the kora. Swayambhunath crowns a hill west of the city with valley views, a 365-step eastern stairway and resident monkeys.

highlights.title: Himalayan sunrise from Nagarkot
highlights.text: From the ridge at about 2,175 m, clear October to February mornings show peaks from Langtang and Dorje Lakpa to Gauri Shankar, and a small tip of Everest on the best days. It is 1.5 hours from Kathmandu, so one night is enough.

highlights.title: Everest mountain flight
highlights.text: A one-hour dawn flight in a pressurised plane from Kathmandu's domestic terminal runs along the Himalaya to Everest and back, with every passenger at a window. There is no landing, and flights depend on clear weather, so we keep a spare morning in the plan.

highlights.title: Newar food and crafts
highlights.text: Bhaktapur's juju dhau yoghurt, Kathmandu's momo and bara, Patan's metal workshops and Bhaktapur's Pottery Square show the valley's Newar culture at street level. Food walks and short pottery or cooking classes fit easily into any city itinerary.

getting_there: Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu receives direct flights from Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Kolkata and Varanasi, among other Indian cities, with flight times of 1 to 2.5 hours, plus connections via the Gulf, Doha, Istanbul, Bangkok, Kuala Lumpur and Singapore. By road, Indian travellers cross most often at Sunauli–Bhairahawa (about 280 km and 8 to 9 hours to Kathmandu), Raxaul–Birgunj (about 270 km, 7 to 8 hours via the Hetauda–Kathmandu roads) or Kakarbhitta in the east. Indian-registered cars need a Bhansar customs permit at the border. Inside the valley we use private cars with drivers, as public buses are slow and crowded. Kathmandu traffic is heavy between 9 and 11 am and 5 and 7 pm, so allow extra time for airport transfers and for flights to Pokhara, Bharatpur and Lukla.
permits: No trekking or area permits are needed to tour the Kathmandu Valley. You pay entry fees at the heritage zones, roughly NPR 1,000 for foreigners at Kathmandu and Patan Durbar Squares and NPR 1,800 at Bhaktapur, with lower SAARC rates for Indians. Indian nationals need a passport or voter ID; other nationalities buy a visa on arrival (US$ 30 for 15 days). The valley rim trek through Shivapuri Nagarjun National Park needs a park entry ticket. Check current status before you travel.

months.weather: Kathmandu 2 to 19 °C, dry, foggy mornings, clear afternoons
months.summary: January is the coldest month, with morning fog in the valley that usually burns off by 10 or 11 am and leaves crisp, clear afternoons. Mountain views from Nagarkot and Chandragiri are often excellent, though sunrise there is close to freezing. Crowds are thin, hotel rates are lower and the heritage squares are pleasant for walking in the midday sun. Early flights, including Everest mountain flights, are sometimes delayed by fog.
months.tip: Plan heritage walks from 10 am to 4 pm, when the fog has lifted and the sun is warm.

months.summary: February warms quickly and brings some of the clearest skies of the year. Days are comfortable for long walks through Patan and Bhaktapur, and the hills give sharp sunrise views. Maha Shivaratri often falls in February or early March, filling Pashupatinath with sadhus and pilgrims from India and Nepal. Book Kathmandu hotels early if your dates overlap Shivaratri, and pack a warm layer for evenings.
months.tip: If you are visiting for Shivaratri, arrive two days early to see the sadhu camps before the main crowds.

months.weather: Kathmandu 8 to 25 °C, mostly dry, some haze later in the month
months.summary: March is warm, dry and good for every kind of valley trip. Rhododendrons start to bloom on the rim hills around Chandragiri and Shivapuri, and the valley rim trek is very pleasant. Haze builds late in the month and can soften mountain views, so plan sunrise viewpoints for the first half. Shivaratri sometimes falls in early March, and Holi colours the streets around the full moon.
months.tip: Book Nagarkot or Dhulikhel sunrises in the first half of March, before spring haze thickens.

months.weather: Kathmandu 11 to 28 °C, warm, occasional evening storms
months.summary: April is warm and busy, with Nepali New Year in mid-April and Bhaktapur's Bisket Jatra chariot festival around it. Afternoons can reach 28 °C, and short thunderstorms sometimes roll in during the evening. Mountain views are hazier than in autumn, but the festival atmosphere and long days make up for it. Indian school holidays start late in the month, so hotel demand rises.
months.tip: Stay a night in Bhaktapur during Bisket Jatra to see the chariot pulling after the day visitors leave.

months.weather: Kathmandu 16 to 29 °C, hot afternoons, pre-monsoon storms
months.summary: May is the hottest month before the monsoon, with humid afternoons and growing cloud. Pre-monsoon storms are common in the evening, and mountain views are mostly hazy, so we focus on temples, museums and shaded courtyards. Buddha Jayanti, the Buddha's birthday, usually falls in May and brings butter lamps and processions to Boudhanath and Swayambhunath. Indian family travel peaks with the summer holidays.
months.tip: Start sightseeing at 7.30 or 8 am and rest in the hotel through the hottest hours.

months.weather: Kathmandu 19 to 29 °C, monsoon starts mid-month, humid
months.summary: The monsoon usually reaches Kathmandu in mid-June. Rain falls mostly in the afternoon and at night, so mornings can still be used for city sightseeing, but mountain views are rare and roads to Pokhara and Chitwan see landslide delays. Hotel rates drop and squares are quiet. We suggest short Kathmandu city breaks and temple circuits rather than mountain-view trips in this month.
months.tip: Carry a compact umbrella and quick-dry shoes, and plan indoor sights such as Patan Museum for afternoons.

months.weather: Kathmandu 20 to 29 °C, heavy monsoon rain, cloudy
months.summary: July is the wettest month, with frequent heavy rain and cloud sitting on the valley rim. Leeches appear on forest trails and highway travel is slow because of landslides. The valley is green and cultural sites remain open, so short city trips are still possible for travellers who accept rain. The Everest mountain flight is often cancelled in cloud, and hill viewpoints rarely show peaks.
months.tip: Keep a flexible day in the plan, as monsoon rain can delay drives and flights.

months.summary: August remains wet, though rain often eases into showers by late in the month. Festivals begin to pick up: Gai Jatra brings cow processions through Kathmandu and Bhaktapur, and Krishna Janmashtami draws devotees to Patan's Krishna Mandir. Indra Jatra sometimes begins at the end of August. Mountain views are still unlikely, and travel beyond the valley should allow for road delays.
months.tip: Plan Patan's Krishna Mandir visit for Janmashtami night if your dates allow, with a guide for the crowds.

months.summary: September is a shoulder month as the monsoon retreats. Showers continue in the first half, but skies clear more often towards the end of the month and the valley is lush. Indra Jatra fills Kathmandu Durbar Square with masked dances and the Kumari chariot procession. Dashain sometimes starts in late September, which affects transport and hotel availability across Nepal.
months.tip: Book late-September trips with one spare day in case late monsoon rain delays a drive or flight.

months.summary: October is peak season, with clear post-monsoon air, comfortable temperatures and the best chance of mountain views from Nagarkot, Dhulikhel and the Everest mountain flight. Dashain usually falls in October, bringing kites, swings and family gatherings, with some shop closures and full buses. Hotels and flights fill early, especially during Indian Durga Puja and Diwali holidays, so book eight weeks or more ahead.
months.tip: Book Nagarkot hotels and Everest mountain flights early, as October demand is the highest of the year.

months.summary: November has the most reliable visibility of the year, with dry days, crisp mornings and cold nights on the hills. Tihar, the festival of lights, usually falls in early November, when Kathmandu's lanes glow with oil lamps on Laxmi Puja night. It is an excellent month for sunrise viewpoints, the valley rim trek and the Everest mountain flight. Bring a warm jacket for Nagarkot dawns near 3 to 5 °C.
months.tip: Walk Asan and Patan's lanes after 7 pm on Laxmi Puja night to see Tihar lamps at their best.

months.weather: Kathmandu 3 to 20 °C, dry, clear, cold mornings
months.summary: December stays dry and clear, with sunny days around 18 to 20 °C and cold mornings near 3 °C in the valley and close to freezing on the hills. Mountain views remain sharp, crowds fall after mid-month and hotel rates are lower than in October. It suits Indian winter-holiday travellers and Christmas and New Year breaks, with the warm sun making heritage walks comfortable.
months.tip: Pack thermal layers for sunrise viewpoints and choose heated rooms at Nagarkot or Dhulikhel.

faqs.q: How many days are enough for Kathmandu Valley?
faqs.a: Three nights is the sweet spot for most first visits: one day for Kathmandu Durbar Square, Swayambhunath and Pashupatinath, one for Patan and Boudhanath, and one for Bhaktapur with Nagarkot or Changunarayan. Two nights covers the highlights at a brisk pace. Add a fourth night for Dhulikhel, Namobuddha or the Everest mountain flight with a weather back-up.

faqs.q: What is the Kathmandu tour package cost from India?
faqs.a: A 3-night Kathmandu city break with a 3-star hotel, private transfers, sightseeing and a guide costs from about ₹16,000 per person twin sharing, excluding flights. Kathmandu with Pokhara for 5 nights starts around ₹24,000, and Kathmandu–Pokhara–Chitwan for 6 nights around ₹32,000. Return flights from Delhi typically add ₹10,000 to 20,000 depending on season.

faqs.q: Do Indians need a passport to visit Kathmandu?
faqs.a: No. Indian citizens can enter Nepal with either a valid Indian passport or an Election Commission voter ID card, and no visa is needed. Aadhaar is not reliably accepted, especially by airlines, so do not rely on it. Children have separate rules, such as school identity certificates for ages 15 to 18. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Kathmandu Valley?
faqs.a: October and November are best, with clear skies, mountain views and comfortable days around 23 to 26 °C. February to April is also good, warmer, with rhododendrons and festivals such as Bisket Jatra, though spring haze softens the views. December and January are clear but cold in the mornings. June to August brings monsoon rain and hidden peaks.

faqs.q: Can you see Mount Everest from Kathmandu?
faqs.a: Not from the city itself. On very clear mornings a distant tip of Everest can be seen from Nagarkot's view tower and some points on the valley rim, mainly from October to December. For a close view, take the one-hour Everest mountain flight from Kathmandu, a fixed-wing plane that flies along the range at about 7,600 m with every passenger at a window.

faqs.q: Is Kathmandu safe for tourists in 2026?
faqs.a: Kathmandu is generally safe for visitors, with petty theft in crowds the most common problem. Street protests and general strikes do occur; in September 2025 protests led to curfews and serious damage to some buildings, including hotels. Situations change, so check current advisories before you travel, avoid demonstrations, and follow your guide's and hotel's advice.

faqs.q: Which UNESCO sites are in Kathmandu Valley?
faqs.a: The Kathmandu Valley World Heritage Site, inscribed in 1979, has seven monument zones: Kathmandu Durbar Square (Hanuman Dhoka), Patan Durbar Square, Bhaktapur Durbar Square, Swayambhunath, Boudhanath, Pashupatinath and Changu Narayan. All seven can be visited in two to three days by car with a guide. Each charges its own entry fee, with lower SAARC rates for Indians.

faqs.q: Is Nagarkot or Dhulikhel better for a sunrise view?
faqs.a: Nagarkot, at about 2,175 m, gives the wider panorama, from Langtang and Dorje Lakpa to Gauri Shankar, and a speck of Everest on the best days. Dhulikhel, at about 1,550 m, is warmer, has a Newar old town and links to Namobuddha and Panauti. Pick Nagarkot for views alone and Dhulikhel for a gentler mix of culture and mountains.

faqs.q: What are the entry fees at Kathmandu Valley heritage sites?
faqs.a: For foreign nationals, roughly NPR 1,000 each at Kathmandu and Patan Durbar Squares and Pashupatinath, NPR 1,800 at Bhaktapur, around NPR 400 at Boudhanath, NPR 200 at Swayambhunath and NPR 300 at Changunarayan. SAARC nationals, including Indians, pay much less, and Hindu pilgrims enter Pashupatinath free for darshan. Check current status before you travel.
